Specification: TLAPS module of induction principles over the naturals: NatInduction, DownwardNatInduction, GeneralNatInduction (course-of-values), SmallestNatural (least-number principle), recursion theorems for functions on Nat (RecursiveFcnOfNat, NatInductiveDef and Type/Unique variants), and analogous theorems on finite intervals m..n. Includes an example using factorial.

IF i = 0 THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[i-1], i)
IF i = m THEN c ELSE Def(g[i-1], i)
IF i = m THEN c ELSE Def(f[i-1], i)
IF n = 0 THEN 1 ELSE n * factorial[n-1]
FunctionConstructor: [i \in Nat |-> IF i = 0 THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[i-1], i)]
[i \in Nat |-> IF i = 0 THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[i-1], i)]
[i \in m..n |-> IF i = m THEN c ELSE Def(g[i-1], i)]
[i \in m..n |-> IF i = m THEN c ELSE Def(f[i-1], i)]
ChoiceExpr: CHOOSE g : g = [i \in Nat |-> IF i = 0 THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[i-1], i)]
CHOOSE g : g = [i \in m..n |-> IF i = m THEN c ELSE Def(g[i-1], i)]
AssumeProveBlocks: ASSUME NEW P(_), P(0), \A n \in Nat : P(n) => P(n+1) PROVE \A n \in Nat : P(n)
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW m \in Nat, P(m), \A n \in 1 .. m : P(n) => P(n-1) PROVE P(0)
ASSUME NEW P(_), \A n \in Nat : (\A m \in 0..(n-1) : P(m)) => P(n) PROVE \A n \in Nat : P(n)
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW n \in Nat, P(n) PROVE \E m \in Nat : /\ P(m) /\ \A k \in 0 .. m-1 : ~ P(k)
ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), ASSUME NEW n \in Nat, NEW g, NEW h, \A i \in 0..(n-1) : g[i] = h[i] PROVE Def(g, n) = Def(h, n) PROVE LET f[n \in Nat] == Def(f, n) IN f = [n \in Nat |-> Def(f, n)]
ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW f0, NatInductiveDefHypothesis(f, f0, Def) PROVE NatInductiveDefConclusion(f, f0, Def)
ASSUME NEW f, NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), f = [n \in Nat |-> Def(f,n)], ASSUME NEW n \in Nat, NEW g, \A i \in 0 .. n-1 : g[i] \in S PROVE Def(g,n) \in S PROVE f \in [Nat -> S]
ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), NEW S, NEW f, NEW f0 \in S, NatInductiveDefConclusion(f, f0, Def), f0 \in S, \A v \in S, n \in Nat \ {0} : Def(v, n) \in S PROVE f \in [Nat -> S]

ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW g, f = [n \in Nat |-> Def(f,n)], g = [n \in Nat |-> Def(g,n)], ASSUME NEW n \in Nat, NEW ff, NEW gg, \A i \in 0..(n-1) : ff[i] = gg[i] PROVE Def(ff, n) = Def(gg, n) PROVE f = g
ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW g, NEW f0, NatInductiveDefConclusion(f, f0, Def), NatInductiveDefConclusion(g, f0, Def) PROVE f = g
ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW c, NEW m \in Nat, NEW n \in Nat, FiniteNatInductiveDefHypothesis(f, c, Def, m, n) PROVE FiniteNatInductiveDefConclusion(f, c, Def, m, n)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW c \in S, NEW m \in Nat, NEW n \in Nat, FiniteNatInductiveDefConclusion(f, c, Def, m, n), \A v \in S, i \in (m+1) .. n : Def(v,i) \in S PROVE f \in [m..n -> S]
ASSUME NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW g, NEW c, NEW m \in Nat, NEW n \in Nat, FiniteNatInductiveDefConclusion(f, c, Def, m, n), FiniteNatInductiveDefConclusion(g, c, Def, m, n) PROVE f = g
